data.summary: ADMIS says Dec meal rose $5–7/st to its highest in five weeks after NOPA showed a low 46.6 lb/bu meal yield, while Dec soybean oil fell more than 1¢/lb to a nine-month low; Pro Farmer has March meal +$6.20 to $351.40, March oil −125 points to 58.80¢ and Jan soybeans +5¼¢ to $12.34. Dec SRW wheat fell 7¼¢ to $5.69¾.
data.title: CBOT 24 Nov: soybean meal leads to a 5-week high, soybean oil hits a 9-month low

data.act: Lock Dec–Jan needs this week with at least two crushers holding bean stocks before they reprice to a CBOT meal price now near $350/st; a licence lapse at end-November would tighten local supply further.
data.why: CBOT meal kept climbing on 24 Nov: Dec rose $5–7/st to a five-week high (ADMIS) and March gained $6.20 to $351.40 (Pro Farmer), on top of the $345.70 Dec settle of 23 Nov, after NOPA showed a low 46.6 lb/bu meal yield; Jan soybeans rose 5¼¢ to $12.34. Pakistan still buys meal from local crushers only: import approvals were deferred on 23 Oct and current GM soybean licences run only through November 2026, with no renewal found as of 25 Nov.

data.act: Buy only for formulas that need it, 15–30 days at a time, and ask local refiners to pass on the lower world price before booking.
data.why: CBOT soybean oil has lost its biofuel support: Dec fell more than 1¢/lb to a nine-month low on 24 Nov (ADMIS) and March closed at 58.80¢, an eight-month low (Pro Farmer), down from about 64.65¢ at end-October. At Rs65 maize and Rs135 SBM its energy is worth about Rs125/kg, so oil remains a pellet-quality and energy-density buy, not a cheap energy buy.

data.note: Jan-27 closed $12.34 on 24 Nov, +5¼¢, after a three-week high early in the session on meal-led buying. Weekly change shown is for the week to 20 Nov.
Dec-26 SRW closed $5.69¾ on 24 Nov, −7¼¢; KC HRW Dec −8¾¢ to $6.12½. Weekly change shown is for the week to 20 Nov.

data.refreshNote: CBOT 24 Nov closes added for soybeans ($12.34, +5¼¢) and SRW wheat ($5.69¾, −7¼¢) with meal at a five-week high and soybean oil at a nine-month low (soybean and soy-oil views refreshed); maize on Kissan Cares is still 23 Nov and wheat 24 Nov, rice rows are generic paddy, Dec corn, Dec meal and Dec oil 24 Nov settles were not confirmed by an exact source, and Brownfield's closing page could not be fetched.
